title: Adaptive parameter schema synthesis and user-friendly validation errors for function/tool calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem summary: Our current function/tool parameter validation is brittle for two reasons: 1) models emit slightly varied JSON shapes (strings instead of integers, optional fields omitted), and 2) our error messages are low-signal, making it hard for SDKs and customers to remediate. This ticket proposes an adaptive schema synthesis layer plus a user-friendly error classification and remediation hints system. The goal is to reduce invalid-call error rates by 40% for top 50 customer prompts while preserving strictness for security-sensitive calls.
proposal: Introduce an intermediary parameter schema representation (PSR) that augments JSON Schema with runtime coercion modes, shallow-fallback rules, and a compact error code set. The PSR will be produced from model-facing tool manifests and from legacy call manifests via a compatibility adaptor. Validation will run in three phases: 1) parse/coerce (best-effort coercions according to policy), 2) strict-type check (required/forbidden fields, patterns), 3) recovery suggestions generation (field-level hints paired with remediation actions). Errors will be mapped to a small set of machine-readable codes and human-readable messages with example fixes. SDKs will receive both the error code and the suggested delta (e.g., "convert field_count to integer: '3' -> 3") so clients can attempt automatic repair before surfacing to users.
design_notes:
- PSR extends JSON Schema with these new attributes: 'coercion': ['none'|'lenient'|'numeric-as-string'], 'accept_null_as_missing': boolean, 'suggested_casts': list-of-strings, 'confidence_hint': ['high'|'medium'|'low'].
- Backward-compat: legacy manifests without PSR will be translated with conservative defaults (coercion: none, accept_null_as_missing: false).
- Error taxonomy: INVALID_TYPE (with expected/received), MISSING_REQUIRED, DEPRECATED_FIELD, ENUM_MISMATCH, EXTRA_FIELD_BLOCKED, CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, COERCION_FAILED. Each error will include a 'repair' suggestion string and an optional 'example' value.
- Telemetry: emit event per validation attempt with fields: manifest_id, call_key_hash, error_codes, coercion_applied (list), latency_ms, resolution_action (auto_fix|client_fix|failed).
validation_flow: 1) Run parser to normalize JSON (strip padding, unescape). 2) Apply declared coercions in PSR in order: numeric-as-string -> trimmed numeric parse; lenient -> try JSON parse sub-strings; none -> skip. 3) Run structural checks and required field checks. 4) Produce error bundle: top-level error code(s), per-field diagnostics, and a suggested repair patch (JSON Patch string). 5) If auto-fix policy enabled (per-customer flag), apply the patch and re-validate; emit telemetry of fixes applied.
acceptance_criteria: PSR is specified and documented in the runtime spec doc (doc link appended in comments).
Runtime implements PSR parsing and the three-phase validation pipeline behind a feature flag.
Error bundle format stable (code, message, field_path, repair_hint, example).
SDKs (python/js/go) can surface repair_hint and optionally auto-apply fixes for the top 3 error classes.
Integration tests show <= 40% reduction in invalid-call errors for top 50 production prompts when lenient mode enabled.
Telemetry schema defined and backfilled for one month of validation events in staging.
tasks: Spec: finalize PSR schema attributes and map to JSON Schema equivalence (owner: Aisha, estimate: 2)
Runtime: implement PSR parser, coercion library, and error bundling (owner: Miguel, estimate: 5)
Compat adapter: translator from legacy manifests to PSR with conservative defaults (owner: Lena, estimate: 3)
SDK changes: expose error bundle and auto-fix helper (owner: SDK team, estimate: 4)
E2E tests: create test corpus of common model-generated malformations and run A/B (owner: QA, estimate: 3)
Telemetry: add validation events to observability pipeline and dashboard (owner: Infra, estimate: 2)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Lenient coercion could mask data integrity bugs or allow incorrect values into downstream systems. Mitigation: add customer-level policy 'auto_fix_policy' with modes (off|warn|apply) and a strict mode that rejects any coercion for 'security' tagged manifests. Add audit log entries when coercion occurs. Risk: performance overhead. Mitigation: cache compiled PSR and reuse compiled validators, limit coercion attempts per-field to small constant, and run costly heuristics off the hot path where possible.
migration_rollout_plan: 1) Phase 0: Spec and static compatibility adapter; feature flag only. 2) Phase 1: Enable PSR parsing in staging for 10% of internal traffic; collect telemetry. 3) Phase 2: Expose SDK helpers for repair hints; opt-in beta customers. 4) Phase 3: Gradual ramp with customer opt-in default to 'warn' coercion. 5) Phase 4: Evaluate metrics and consider making lenient mode default for public hosted API. Each phase gated by error rate, customer complaints, and telemetry quality metrics.
